title: A workspace test run publishes a worktree binary's own root as the machine's install pointer, and every estate's gate then runs that tree's guards silently
body:
A workspace test run under the operator's real HOME lets a worktree binary publish its own root as the machine's install pointer, and every estate's pre-commit gate then resolves its guards from that scratch tree without saying so.

**Seen 2026-09-19.** `~/.local/share/intent/home` was rewritten at 16:17:33Z to `.../scratchpad/wt-0481base`, a private worktree, inside a `cargo build -p intentd && cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` run there (16:16:23Z to 16:20:06Z). That run, and every whole-suite run ic made that day, used the ambient environment: HOME=/Users/matts, no XDG_* set. The release gate sets HOME to a private directory for the same cargo line (bin/.devbin/cmd/build.d/release:730); a hand-run copy of the line does not. Devbin's, dc's and cc's commits after 16:17Z ran their guards from that worktree, which was main at 35b902fd9 without T3. Earlier whole-suite runs from other worktrees that day may have published their roots the same way in their own windows.

**The writer, named.** Only `intent bootstrap` writes the pointer (render.rs `bootstrap`, `intentsvcs::bootstrap::run`, `install::publish_home`), and it publishes the RUNNING binary's own root. The arm is intent-cli's separate test target `dual_path_conformance` (tests/dual_path_conformance.rs; its own `[[test]]` in intent-cli/Cargo.toml, outside the one `suite` target), in `invariant_every_shipped_verb_answers_identically_down_every_route`. Its in-process route `via_library` calls `intent_cli::dispatch` in the test process for every shipped verb that `HAZARDS` does not refuse, and `bootstrap` is not in `HAZARDS` (the daemon, app, discover, explore and mcp rows are). So `bootstrap` runs in-process under the test process's real HOME, `install::home()` resolves the test binary's own worktree, and `publish_home` writes it. `via_binary` is isolated through `testkit::fixture_home`; the in-process route cannot be, which is what `Hazard::ActsOnAmbientUserState` exists to declare. `testkit::fixture_home` itself exists because two `dispatch_ssot` arms published a scratch worktree on 2026-08-27, so this is the class's second firing.

**Evidence.** In one worktree's build, each run under a fresh sentinel HOME: `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` wrote `<sentinel>/.local/share/intent/home` naming that worktree; each of the nine test binaries run alone under its own sentinel, and only `dual_path_conformance` wrote it (intent-cli's lib and suite, intentd's three targets, intentsvcs's lib and suite and testkit's suite left it empty). The machine's real pointer was untouched throughout.

**The probe (a second defect).** `intent claude upgrade` WITHOUT `--apply` prints no "different install" note while the pointer names another tree (measured by devbin-vc: grep counts 0); the note appears only on `--apply`. The dry run is silent in exactly the state the note exists to report.

**Fix candidates:**
1. `("bootstrap", &[Hazard::ActsOnAmbientUserState])` in `dual_path_conformance`'s `HAZARDS`, the declared exclusion its siblings already use.
2. `install::publish_home` refuses a root that is a linked git worktree (`--git-dir` differing from `--git-common-dir`) or lies under the system temporary directory, naming the root and the remedy, so the next arm that forgets cannot redirect the machine.
3. `claude upgrade`'s dry run prints the "different install" note whenever the pointer differs from the running binary's root, exactly as `--apply` does.
4. Every intent-cli arm that spawns the binary does so through `testkit::fixture_home` by construction.

Severity high: while the pointer names a scratch tree, every estate's pre-commit gate runs guards nobody reviewed for that estate, and nothing says so. M.


**CLOSED on four fixes, and the refusal is narrower than the one first written.** (1) `("bootstrap", &[Hazard::ActsOnAmbientUserState])` joins `dual_path_conformance`'s HAZARDS, so the in-process route no longer drives it. (2) `install::publish_home` refuses to let a SCRATCH root replace a pointer that already names a real install. (3) `claude upgrade`'s dry run prints the different-install note, through one helper both routes call; the two `CANNOT RUN` warnings stay on the apply path, because those qualify a gate that was just installed while the note describes the machine. (4) `upgrade_command.rs` spawns through `testkit::fixture_home`; the rest of that sweep is its own issue, named below.

**The first shape of (2) refused every scratch root outright, and it was wrong twice over** (vc's ruling of 2026-09-20, taken after the first bank came back red). It would have refused a fresh machine, a CI runner and gyges, none of which has anything better to publish; and because the root `publish_home` resolves is the RUNNING binary's own, it made `intent bootstrap` refuse from ANY worktree checkout, reddening six `bootstrap_door` arms and one of `a_fresh_project_commits_clean` -- turning a suite's verdict into a function of where the checkout lives. So the subject moved from the root's nature to the REPLACEMENT: a real install silently replaced by a scratch one is refused, and everything else publishes as before. A pointer that is absent, empty, naming a root that no longer exists, or already naming a scratch root takes any candidate -- and that last clause is what lets this machine's hijacked pointer be repaired by an ordinary `intent bootstrap` from the tree it should have named. The seven arms are green untouched.

**The shape, PFIC.** `scratch_within(root, temps, gitdir)` classifies a root and `replacement_refused(candidate, candidate_scratch, existing, existing_scratch, existing_exists)` decides; both are pure, take every input as a parameter, and are driven to every verdict without a filesystem, including the four allowing clauses and a submodule control. `scratch` reads the machine's answers for them and `publish_home_at` calls the decision. The worktree test reads the `.git` FILE's `gitdir:` line rather than running `git`, so it needs no subprocess and no readable repository, and the `worktrees` path component is what separates a linked worktree from a submodule, whose `.git` is also a file. One error, `WouldReplaceARealInstall`, names the existing root, the candidate and why, with a remedy stating the pointer was KEPT and giving both deliberate paths.

**The mechanism was reproduced before it was fixed, and the instrument is the pointer file itself.** Under a sentinel HOME whose pointer file was truncated to empty before each run, with the HAZARDS entry and the refusal both reverted, `cargo test -p intent-cli --test dual_path_conformance` published the running worktree's own root into `<sentinel>/.local/share/intent/home` -- and reported `ok`, which is the defect's signature rather than an aside: a conformance check compares answers and cannot see a side effect. With the refusal alone restored the file stayed empty, so the two fixes are independent and either one stops the write. Every run in the judged bank left it empty, and the machine's real pointer was untouched throughout.

**What the redirected pointer actually changed, measured by cc and vc rather than assumed.** At Intent nothing: the gate resolves its body through the pointer and that body was byte-identical to main's, while the guard bodies come from this repository whatever the pointer names (`lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit.sh:188-196`). Every commit gated here ran main's gate and main's guards. It is the other estates, which load both the gate and its guards from the named worktree, that ran the pre-T3 bodies of `append-only-guard.sh` and `pre-commit-guards.sh`.

**What the integration arm cannot see, said plainly.** `bootstrap_door`'s fixture HOME is built under the system temporary directory, so the "real" root it seeds is itself scratch on every machine, and the candidate is scratch in a bank worktree and not on a plain checkout. Both cases therefore take the ALLOWING branch: the arm proves the verb runs, publishes and agrees with the classifier, and it never exercises the refusing branch anywhere. The refusal's both-verdicts coverage is the pure arms alone. An earlier draft of that arm asserted the seeded root was real, which would have been green in a bank worktree and red on a plain checkout -- the very shape this issue's ruling rejects -- so it was removed and the limit written down instead.

**What this does NOT fix, and where it went: issue 0493.** The spawns themselves are unchanged. Of the intent-cli test files that spawn the binary, 47 still set no HOME at all and inherit the operator's, three of them naming a verb already declared as acting on ambient user state. The pointer is closed against them regardless, because the refusal lives in `publish_home` rather than in any spawn -- so what remains is the project registry that issue 0445 records, the state directory, the daemon socket and log, and the config. That sweep, and the mechanism that would keep it true (a guard arm naming every unfixtured spawn, or a `testkit` spawn helper that cannot be called without a HOME), is issue 0493.
